text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis: Reference definitions for the five-point Kellgren-Lawrence (KL) scale used by the KneeXpert radiographic pipeline. Written for this project because published research articles cite the KL scale constantly but rarely restate its criteria plainly, which leaves a retrieval corpus of literature unable to ground a statement as basic as what grade 2 means.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Grade 0 — Normal: No radiographic features of osteoarthritis. Joint space is preserved with no osteophyte formation. There is no subchondral sclerosis and no abnormality of bone contour. A grade 0 radiograph does not exclude soft-tissue pathology: cartilage damage, meniscal tears and ligament injury are not visible on plain radiography and require magnetic resonance imaging to assess.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Grade 1 — Doubtful: Doubtful joint space narrowing, with possible early osteophytic lipping at the tibial spines. No definite subchondral change is present. The boundary between grade 0 and grade 1 is the least reproducible point on the scale, and inter-observer agreement is lowest here. A grade 1 reading should be treated as uncertain rather than as evidence of early disease, and correlated with symptoms before any management decision.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Grade 2 — Mild: Definite osteophytes are identified, typically at the tibial plateau and the femoral condyles. Joint space narrowing may be present, most often in the medial compartment. Mild subchondral bone change may be visible but without established sclerosis. Grade 2 is the threshold conventionally used to define the presence of radiographic osteoarthritis in epidemiological work.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Grade 3 — Moderate: Definite joint space narrowing, usually medial. Osteophyte formation is present at multiple margins, which may include the tibial plateau, the femoral condyles and the patella. Subchondral sclerosis is detectable, characteristically in the medial tibial plateau. Some deformity of bone contour may be apparent.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Grade 4 — Severe: Marked joint space narrowing, which may extend to bone-on-bone contact in the medial compartment. Large osteophytes are present at all compartment margins. Subchondral sclerosis is established and subchondral cyst formation may be present. There is definite deformity of bone contour, commonly flattening of the femoral condyle.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

section_path: Features the scale is built from
text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Features the scale is built from: Four radiographic features determine a KL grade. Osteophytes are bony outgrowths at the joint margins and are the earliest reliably-visible feature. Joint space narrowing is the indirect radiographic signature of cartilage loss, since cartilage itself is radiolucent. Subchondral sclerosis is increased bone density beneath the articular surface, appearing later than osteophytosis. Bone contour deformity is the latest feature and indicates structural collapse of the joint line.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis — Reliability and interpretation limits: KL grading is a reading of structure, not of symptoms, and the correlation between radiographic grade and reported pain is weak. Inter-observer variance is substantial, concentrated at the grade 0 to grade 1 and grade 1 to grade 2 transitions. A grade assigned from a single projection is less reliable than one assigned from a weight-bearing view, because joint space width depends on load. Automated grading systems exhibit their lowest accuracy at the same boundaries that challenge human readers, so a borderline automated grade carries the uncertainty of both the model and the scale. Radiographic grade alone is not a sufficient basis for a surgical decision, and a normal radiograph does not exclude a symptomatic soft-tissue injury.
title: Kellgren-Lawrence radiographic grading of knee osteoarthritis

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories: Definitions for the sixteen multi-label categories the KneeXpert MRI pipeline predicts, matching backend/mri/categories.json exactly. Written for this project because the label names are dataset shorthand: published literature describes these pathologies at length but never under these exact names, so a corpus of research articles alone cannot ground a statement about what a given predicted label means. Categories are not mutually exclusive. A single study commonly carries several, and the SKM-TEA annotations average roughly 2.4 labels per study.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Meniscal tear patterns: The meniscus is a fibrocartilaginous structure distributing load across the tibiofemoral joint. Tear morphology determines whether a tear is mechanically significant and whether it is repairable. Meniscal Tear (Myxoid) — myxoid degeneration signal within the meniscal substance, without a discrete tear plane reaching a surface. Generally a degenerative finding rather than an acute injury. Meniscal Tear (Horizontal) — a horizontal cleavage plane splitting the meniscus into upper and lower leaves. Typically degenerative. Meniscal Tear (Radial) — a tear running perpendicular to the circumferential fibres, extending toward or reaching the capsular junction. Because it severs the load-distributing fibres, a radial tear compromises hoop-stress function disproportionately to its size. Meniscal Tear (Vertical/Longitudinal) — a tear running along the circumferential fibres.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Meniscal tear patterns: Preserves hoop stress better than a radial tear and is more often repairable. Meniscal Tear (Oblique) — an oblique tear plane, sometimes described as a parrot-beak configuration, with features of both radial and longitudinal patterns. Meniscal Tear (Complex) — tearing in multiple planes. Associated with a higher risk of mechanical symptoms and less amenable to repair. Meniscal Tear (Flap) — a tear producing a displaced fragment. The displaced flap can cause catching or locking. Meniscal Tear (Extrusion) — displacement of meniscal tissue beyond the tibial plateau margin. Indicates root detachment or radial deficiency and is strongly associated with progression of cartilage loss.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Ligament injury grades: Graded by the degree of fibre disruption, which determines whether the ligament remains functionally competent. Ligament Tear (Low-Grade Sprain) — fibres intact with mild abnormal signal. Functionally competent. Ligament Tear (Moderate Grade Sprain or Mucoid Degeneration) — partial fibre disruption, or mucoid degeneration of the ligament substance. Partially competent. Ligament Tear (Full Thickness/Complete Tear) — complete discontinuity of fibres. The ligament is functionally incompetent, with implications for joint stability.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Cartilage lesion grades: A depth-based scale. Depth is the primary determinant of management, because lesions reaching subchondral bone do not heal spontaneously. Cartilage Lesion (1) — signal change with an intact articular surface, corresponding to softening or fibrillation. Cartilage Lesion (2A) — superficial partial-thickness defect, extending into the superficial zone only. Cartilage Lesion (2B) — deep partial-thickness defect, extending into the deep zone but not reaching subchondral bone. Cartilage Lesion (3) — full-thickness defect with subchondral bone exposed.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Joint effusion: Effusion — excess synovial fluid within the joint capsule. A non-specific marker of intra-articular pathology or inflammation. Effusion in isolation does not localise a cause, but its presence raises the prior probability that some intra-articular abnormality is present, and its absence does not exclude one.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories

text: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories — Relationship to radiographic grading: These categories describe soft tissue and are therefore largely invisible on plain radiography, which is precisely the diagnostic gap MRI fills. A knee with a normal Kellgren-Lawrence grade can carry a full-thickness cartilage defect or a complete ligament tear. Conversely, advanced radiographic osteoarthritis can coexist with, and visually mask, concurrent soft-tissue pathology. A mapping from these categories to a Kellgren-Lawrence grade is therefore an approximation across different tissue types and should not be read as a radiographic measurement.
title: SKM-TEA diagnostic categories
